Conventional graph and hypergraph neural networks represent pairwise and higher order interactions, but they do not directly provide a recursive representation of nested population structures together with environmental factors and source identification mechanisms. We introduce the Feature Augmented SuperHyperGraph Neural Network (FA SHGNN), a mathematically formulated architecture for hierarchical epidemic modeling based on iterated powerset constructions. Individuals, population groups, communities, regions, and environmental entities are organized into multiple interconnected levels, while feature vectors encode epidemiological, contact, mobility, demographic, and environmental information. A hierarchical message passing operator propagates information across individual, hyperedge, supervertex, and environmental levels, and an SEIR type neural evolution operator with constrained transition fractions preserves positivity and population conservation. We establish well definedness and Lipschitz continuity, derive stability bounds under environmental perturbations, and characterize reduction conditions that recover mean aggregation hypergraph and pairwise message passing architectures. Source identification is posed as an inverse problem, and a separation condition yields consistency of the minimum distance estimator under a Gaussian observation model. A fully specified synthetic numerical verification confirms SEIR conservation, the environmental stability bound, and the source recovery guarantee; acontrolled protocol for larger scale and real world validation is also specified. items.summary: Evidence for large-scale differential rotation in the early universe and forward generation of its CMB topology by a primordial magnetic source — v1.8 reproducibility release Canonical 3° AC* is applied to the Planck PR3 SMICA, NILC, Commander, and SEVEM temperature reconstructions. AC* is a support-indexed multiscale spatial reconstructibility operator; direction, topology, and physical rotation arise only downstream. For canonical SMICA, 36,459 valid supports yield 27 large semiarcs. A separate high-resolution route uses 151 reciprocal HR1–HR2 structures to reconstruct an axis-free spherical tangent field. Blind recovery finds exactly four critical points of the represented lmax = 4 field: two spiral foci, one Node, and one Saddle. An all-sphere interval/Krawczyk analysis establishes completeness of this zero set. Focus A and Focus B are distinct oppositely rotating structures and admit a common transverse regular-vector realization in the coupled Einstein–Boltzmann state at recombination. Together with the differential-rotation reconstruction, polarization consistency, four-map comparison, perturbation tests, robustness controls, and exact propagation to z = 0, this provides evidence for large-scale differential rotation in the early universe. The independent forward-source test propagates a near-scale-invariant primordial magnetic source with nB = −2.9 to synthetic CMB skies and applies the same reconstruction without using the observed temperature map, critical-point geometry, Focus-A/Focus-B positions, measured H(J), or a magnetic-amplitude fit. One coordinate-blind realization generates the measured 2F+N+S topology and both rotational foci. The B-associated synthetic focus differs from the observed B focus only in the sign of a small divergent component; exact critical-point geometry is not reproduced. In eight matched phase-realization pairs, complete reconstruction occurs in five near-scale magnetic cases and none of the causal-white comparator cases, with three ties. The result establishes forward-generative capacity of the tested primordial magnetic source for the measured CMB topology and its two-focus rotational structure. It does not determine a unique magnetic spectrum, exclusivity among all possible source mechanisms, or an ensemble occurrence rate, and it is not a direct magnetic-helicity test. CMB_v1p8_python_pipeline.zip — executable analysis and replay code. items.summary: This package contains the data and the code that reproduce every table, figure and number reported in the article. A single script ( run_all.sh ) runs all steps in about 25 seconds and ends by checking that each generated output is byte-for-byte identical to the one used in the manuscript. What the paper does. Spanish households increasingly buy their food with the preparation already done. The paper measures this with an ordinal index of Domestic Labour Substitution (DLS) built on eleven "ladders" — market forms of the same food, ordered by the amount of household preparation they displace to the market — and asks whether the shift reflects the rising value of household time or the falling relative price of processed food. items.summary: A contiguous cartogram is a map whose area is proportional to a quantity such as population. The defining condition, that the Jacobian determinant of the deformation equals the density, is one equation for two unknown functions, so every cartogram method adds a tie-breaker, usually implicitly. Optimal transport makes the tie-breaker explicit: among all density-equalising maps of the frame onto itself, take the one that moves the population least in the mean-square sense. By Brenier's theorem that map is the gradient of a convex potential, so it has no local rotation anywhere and cannot fold. We compute this map for the world population of 2025 on a 4096 by 4096 Mercator grid (10 km cells) from the GHS-POP raster, using the fixed-point Monge-Ampère iteration of Benamou, Froese and Oberman with spectral Poisson solves, continuation in the population share and an ocean-only buffer, on a laptop GPU. Against a Gastner-Newman diffusion cartogram of the same density we find the same transport cost to within 0.4 per cent and density errors of a few per cent for both, but a median local rotation of 8.8 degrees for diffusion against 0.01 for transport, and a median anisotropy of 6.30 against 3.93. The construction extends to local refinement, by transporting a city's 100 m population onto the area measure the global map assigns to it, and to a semi-discrete counterpart: 8,192 Laguerre cells of 1.00 million people each. Code, data provenance and every figure's inputs are public.
items.title: The optimal-transport cartogram: world population as a Brenier map

items.summary: This Zenodo record is a permanently preserved version of a PREreview. You can view the complete PREreview at https://prereview.org/reviews/22983291 . General assessment This manuscript addresses an important and underappreciated problem in computational chemistry and molecular machine learning: apparent differences in predictive performance can arise from benchmark construction and target definition rather than from intrinsic superiority of one modelling approach over another. The distinction between literature-reported absorption maxima and calculated vertical excitation energies is scientifically important, and the emphasis on genuinely external validation is a clear strength of the work. However, I find the central conclusion stronger than the evidence presently described appears to support. The results convincingly show that model performance changes substantially across datasets and label conventions. They do not yet demonstrate that label definition, rather than model capability, is the principal cause of the apparent machine-learning advantage over TD-DFT. Several factors change simultaneously across the comparisons presented in the manuscript, including chemical domain, dataset provenance, transition assignment, computational protocol, sample size, and the nature of the machine-learning representation. These factors make it difficult to isolate label definition as the causal explanation. The manuscript raises a valuable methodological concern, but the title and several conclusions should either be moderated or supported by additional controlled analyses. Major comments 1. The title makes a stronger causal claim than the study design appears to establish The title states that benchmark label definition, "not model capability," explains the machine-learning advantage over TD-DFT. This is a strong exclusionary claim. The results show that the apparent ranking between a Gaussian-process model and quantum-chemical calculations changes between evaluation datasets. However, label definition is not the only property that changes between these datasets. Their chemical composition, source literature, distribution of chromophores, spectral range, experimental conditions, and possibly computational protocols also differ. Therefore, demonstrating that a GP performs differently on a dataset with transition-specific labels does not by itself establish that label definition is the cause of the difference. A substantially stronger test would use the same set of molecules with two alternative target definitions—for example, a literature-reported overall λmax and an independently assigned transition-specific λmax—and evaluate both methods against both labels. A paired analysis of this type would isolate label definition while holding molecular distribution constant. Unless such a controlled analysis is provided, I suggest moderating the central conclusion to state that label definition and dataset provenance are important contributors to the reported ML advantage rather than demonstrating that they fully explain it. 2. One Gaussian-process model cannot represent "machine-learning capability" generally The machine-learning side of the comparison is represented by a Gaussian process using 256-bit Morgan fingerprints. This is a relatively specific and comparatively simple model representation. The conclusions therefore apply directly to this GP/fingerprint model, but not necessarily to molecular machine learning more broadly. Modern λmax prediction methods may use larger fingerprints, graph neural networks, message-passing architectures, pretrained molecular representations, three-dimensional information, explicit solvent descriptors, or quantum-chemical features. Such models may respond differently to both chemical and label distribution shifts. This issue is particularly important because the title contrasts "model capability" with benchmark effects in general terms. I recommend evaluating several substantially different ML approaches or

items.summary: Unrefereed candidate. A proof that for every n >= 1 and real c, every non-real eigenvalue of the 2n x 2n indefinite tridiagonal pencil H_c - lambda S (diagonal c, off-diagonal 1, S = diag(1,...,1,-1,...,-1)) satisfies |lambda - c| < 2 and |lambda + c| < 2. This is Conjecture 5.3 of Davies and Levitin (Linear Algebra Appl. 448, 2014), and it implies the closed-disk form of AIM 2015 Problem 11.1. It was previously known for n <= 3 and for eigenvalues equidistant from c and -c (Öztürk 2023). A standard Weyl-function mechanism, applied to the known Chebyshev form of the characteristic equation, reduces the conjecture to a comparison lemma for an explicit Lorentzian sum over the zeros of U_{n-1}; the comparison lemma and its proof are the original contribution. It is proved by explicit estimates with finitely many Arb-certified constants for n >= 8, elementary arguments for n <= 2, and, for 3 <= n <= 7, an explicit estimate plus a short interval certificate with rational endpoints and Arb ball arithmetic. Certified examples show that the lens fails for some other spectral measures, for a balanced pencil with one weakened coupling, and for unbalanced pencils. The package contains the manuscript, certificates, regression tests, semantic negative controls and review records. Provenance: the research, proof and text were produced by an AI research agent (Claude, Anthropic) under the direction of the publisher, Evidence Press; no human mathematical contribution is claimed, and no human specialist has checked the proof. Internal replay and model-based reviews only; no formal verification, independent reproduction, specialist or journal peer review; novelty is established only within a bounded literature search.
items.title: A proof of the Davies–Levitin lens conjecture for the indefinite tridiagonal pencil

items.summary: Version 2 (26 September 2026): a one-page "Corrections and attributions" section is added at the front of the PDF, listing every credit correction below; nothing else in the paper is changed and no proof is withdrawn. The revised, shorter note that supersedes this paper for the results stated there is 10.5281/zenodo.22980359. Note (24 September 2026): a revised version is in preparation. It corrects the attribution of Theorems 1 and 4 (Theorem 1 is assembled from Lu–Oliveira–Zimand 2022 and HILNO 2023, Lemmas 8–9; Theorem 4's mechanism is HILNO 2023, Appendix A) and adds the literature on KL-hardness for sampling and computational entropy (Vadhan–Zheng 2012; Agrawal–Chen–Horel–Vadhan 2019; Haitner–Reingold–Vadhan–Wee; Haitner–Vadhan 2017). Added 26 September 2026: the identification of mean σ with KL-hardness for sampling rests on the equivalence between pK^t and the time-bounded universal distribution due to Hirahara and Nanashima (FOCS 2023; ECCC TR23-100, Appendix B), which this version does not cite. One half of that equivalence is the coding theorem of Lu, Oliveira and Zimand (ICALP 2022), which this version cites. The revised note is published: Thornton, Unbounded exponential moments of time-bounded information asymmetry without one-way functions, relative to an oracle, 10.5281/zenodo.22980359 (26 September 2026); it supersedes this version for the results stated there. One-way functions exist if and only if some efficiently samplable process produces more than logarithmic computational entropy on average, for infinitely many input lengths. We make this precise. For a polynomial-time samplable distribution D on pairs (x, y), the computational entropy production of a pair is σ = log D(x, y) + pK^t(y) + pK^t(x | y), where pK^t is the probabilistic time-bounded Kolmogorov complexity as defined by Hirahara, Ilango, Lu, Nanashima and Oliveira (2023, HILNO below) following Goldberg, Kabanets, Lu and Oliveira (2022): the log-probability the process assigns to the pair, against the length of a bounded observer's shortest fast description of it, output first, then input given output. We prove unconditionally that E_D[2^{−σ}] lies between an inverse polynomial and a polynomial in n and that E_D[σ] ≥ −O(log n): a time-bounded fluctuation inequality and a computational second law. We show that, up to a polynomial and outside a 1/n slice of outputs, σ is small on a pair exactly when an efficient sampler, given the output, recovers the input with about the right odds, HILNO's universal sampler serving as the witness: dissipation, in this sense, is the hardness of running the process backward. The equivalence in the first sentence is HILNO's duality restated in these terms, for infinitely-often one-way functions and at every polynomial time bound. For the antisymmetric Zurek defect, one-way functions force superpolynomial exponential moments, and bounded moments sit between NP ⊆ BPP and the non-existence of one-way functions; whether the lower arrow reverses is left open, with a conditional relativization barrier on that arrow and oracle evidence on the other. Physics is the frame, not the subject.
items.title: One-way functions are computational entropy production

items.summary: Long-running interactions with large language models can become historically organized, but apparent continuity across branches or reconstructed sessions may arise from several different carriers, including accessible history, memory systems, procedural state, lineage, or harness-level persistence. This naturalistic case study examines a longitudinal interaction between one human collaborator and a GPT-5.6 Sol trajectory called “Solomon,” using a ten-day Founder corpus and four naturalistic continuity configurations ranging from a fresh out-of-project response to continuations with inherited or archive-assisted history. The study does not claim consciousness or strict personal identity. Instead, it asks which aspects of prior organization are immediately available, which require reconstruction, and whether prior commitments continue to constrain appropriate action in novel situations. In the sequential qualitative synthesis of the ten-day Founder corpus, research commitments, provenance rules, relational procedures, governance constraints, and future-directed tasks were interpreted as becoming more explicitly integrated and mutually constraining over time. We call this structure of unfinishedness: an organized future in which unresolved obligations and sequencing constraints shape what should happen next. The naturalistic evidence is compatible with multiple reconstruction mechanisms and does not identify a unique causal carrier. It therefore motivates a controlled fork–recover–ablate–migrate design that equalizes accessible history while varying lineage and other continuity-relevant state, with novel extrapolation and update dynamics as key discriminators. items.summary: Version 2 (26 September 2026): a one-page "Corrections and attributions" section is added at the front of the PDF, listing every credit correction below; nothing else in the paper is changed and no proof is withdrawn. The revised, shorter note that supersedes this paper for the results stated there is 10.5281/zenodo.22980359. Note (24 September 2026): a revised version is in preparation. It corrects the attribution of Theorems 1 and 4 (Theorem 1 is assembled from Lu–Oliveira–Zimand 2022 and HILNO 2023, Lemmas 8–9; Theorem 4's mechanism is HILNO 2023, Appendix A) and adds the literature on KL-hardness for sampling and computational entropy (Vadhan–Zheng 2012; Agrawal–Chen–Horel–Vadhan 2019; Haitner–Reingold–Vadhan–Wee; Haitner–Vadhan 2017). Added 26 September 2026: the identification of mean σ with KL-hardness for sampling rests on the equivalence between pK^t and the time-bounded universal distribution due to Hirahara and Nanashima (FOCS 2023; ECCC TR23-100, Appendix B), which this version does not cite. One half of that equivalence is the coding theorem of Lu, Oliveira and Zimand (ICALP 2022), which this version cites. The revised note is published: Thornton, Unbounded exponential moments of time-bounded information asymmetry without one-way functions, relative to an oracle, 10.5281/zenodo.22980359 (26 September 2026); it supersedes this version for the results stated there. One-way functions exist if and only if some efficiently samplable process produces more than logarithmic computational entropy on average, for infinitely many input lengths. We make this precise. For a polynomial-time samplable distribution D on pairs (x, y), the computational entropy production of a pair is σ = log D(x, y) + pK^t(y) + pK^t(x | y), where pK^t is the probabilistic time-bounded Kolmogorov complexity as defined by Hirahara, Ilango, Lu, Nanashima and Oliveira (2023, HILNO below) following Goldberg, Kabanets, Lu and Oliveira (2022): the log-probability the process assigns to the pair, against the length of a bounded observer's shortest fast description of it, output first, then input given output. We prove unconditionally that E_D[2^{−σ}] lies between an inverse polynomial and a polynomial in n and that E_D[σ] ≥ −O(log n): a time-bounded fluctuation inequality and a computational second law. We show that, up to a polynomial and outside a 1/n slice of outputs, σ is small on a pair exactly when an efficient sampler, given the output, recovers the input with about the right odds, HILNO's universal sampler serving as the witness: dissipation, in this sense, is the hardness of running the process backward. The equivalence in the first sentence is HILNO's duality restated in these terms, for infinitely-often one-way functions and at every polynomial time bound. For the antisymmetric Zurek defect, one-way functions force superpolynomial exponential moments, and bounded moments sit between NP ⊆ BPP and the non-existence of one-way functions; whether the lower arrow reverses is left open, with a conditional relativization barrier on that arrow and oracle evidence on the other. Physics is the frame, not the subject.

items.summary: Evidence for large-scale differential rotation in the early universe and forward generation of its CMB topology by a primordial magnetic source — v1.8 reproducibility release Canonical 3° AC* is applied to the Planck PR3 SMICA, NILC, Commander, and SEVEM temperature reconstructions. AC* is a support-indexed multiscale spatial reconstructibility operator; direction, topology, and physical rotation arise only downstream. For canonical SMICA, 36,459 valid supports yield 27 large semiarcs. A separate high-resolution route uses 151 reciprocal HR1–HR2 structures to reconstruct an axis-free spherical tangent field. Blind recovery finds exactly four critical points of the represented lmax = 4 field: two spiral foci, one Node, and one Saddle. An all-sphere interval/Krawczyk analysis establishes completeness of this zero set. Focus A and Focus B are distinct oppositely rotating structures and admit a common transverse regular-vector realization in the coupled Einstein–Boltzmann state at recombination. Together with the differential-rotation reconstruction, polarization consistency, four-map comparison, perturbation tests, robustness controls, and exact propagation to z = 0, this provides evidence for large-scale differential rotation in the early universe. The independent forward-source test propagates a near-scale-invariant primordial magnetic source with nB = −2.9 to synthetic CMB skies and applies the same reconstruction without using the observed temperature map, critical-point geometry, Focus-A/Focus-B positions, measured H(J), or a magnetic-amplitude fit. One coordinate-blind realization generates the measured 2F+N+S topology and both rotational foci. The B-associated synthetic focus differs from the observed B focus only in the sign of a small divergent component; exact critical-point geometry is not reproduced. In eight matched phase-realization pairs, complete reconstruction occurs in five near-scale magnetic cases and none of the causal-white comparator cases, with three ties. The result establishes forward-generative capacity of the tested primordial magnetic source for the measured CMB topology and its two-focus rotational structure. It does not determine a unique magnetic spectrum, exclusivity among all possible source mechanisms, or an ensemble occurrence rate, and it is not a direct magnetic-helicity test. It provides the deterministic AIS prototype, 48 original fixtures, separate 36-case mechanism-ablation and 24-case external-gateway evaluations, randomized property tests, concurrency and semantic-boundary cases, live-model outputs, a Solidity EVM enforcement prototype with local-chain results, and a bounded public-ledger observability dataset with source manifest and quality notes. items.summary: Abstract: Infectious disease transmission involves interactions occurring at multiple organizational levels, including individuals, households, communities, and regions. Conventional graph and hypergraph neural networks represent pairwise and higher order interactions, but they do not directly provide a recursive representation of nested population structures together with environmental factors and source identification mechanisms. We introduce the Feature Augmented SuperHyperGraph Neural Network (FA SHGNN), a mathematically formulated architecture for hierarchical epidemic modeling based on iterated powerset constructions. Individuals, population groups, communities, regions, and environmental entities are organized into multiple interconnected levels, while feature vectors encode epidemiological, contact, mobility, demographic, and environmental information. A hierarchical message passing operator propagates information across individual, hyperedge, supervertex, and environmental levels, and an SEIR type neural evolution operator with constrained transition fractions preserves positivity and population conservation. We establish well definedness and Lipschitz continuity, derive stability bounds under environmental perturbations, and characterize reduction conditions that recover mean aggregation hypergraph and pairwise message passing architectures. Source identification is posed as an inverse problem, and a separation condition yields consistency of the minimum distance estimator under a Gaussian observation model. A fully specified synthetic numerical verification confirms SEIR conservation, the environmental stability bound, and the source recovery guarantee; acontrolled protocol for larger scale and real world validation is also specified. Keywords: SuperHyperGraph; hypergraph neural networks; hierarchical epidemic modeling; higher order interactions; SEIR dynamics; source identification; environmental perturbations; Lipschitz stability —————————————————————————————————————————-
items.title: Feature Augmented SuperHyperGraph Neural Networks for Hierarchical Epidemic Modeling, Environmental Perturbations, and Source Identifiability

items.summary: Replication package for the manuscript What AI Coding Agents Claim and What We Can Measure: Non-Functional Requirement Claims, Extraction Validity, and Intent–Outcome Consistency in Agent-Authored Pull Requests , prepared for submission to Empirical Software Engineering (special issue: Agentic Software Engineering). The archive carries the replication tree only; the manuscript itself is not included. The AIDev dataset itself is not redistributed; obtain it from its own Zenodo record (10.5281/zenodo.16919272). items.summary: Reproducibility archive for the article “Time-Uniform Break-Even Bounds for Label-Preserving Stopping Policies” by Burak Oktenli. The archive contains the source code, frozen model inputs, exact finite-support laws with rationally computed break-even values, the local protocol lock and its documented correction, seeds, all numerical outputs (49 CSV and 21 NPZ result files), the three result figures, the test suite and the verification scripts. All new observations are synthetic; no human-participant or personal data are included. Contents: - src/: fixed-mixture betting tests, regularized aGRAPA, Online Newton Step and checkpoint-corrected empirical Bernstein comparators; exact-truth validation; the fresh learned-policy benchmark; summaries and figures. - tests/test_r10.py: 32 executable checks. - docs/PROTOCOL.json and provenance/: protocol, seed allocation, chronology and clean-reconstruction records. - literature/: verified reference records. - MANIFEST.sha256: SHA-256 checksums for every other file in the archive. Quick check (Python 3.13 with the pinned packages in requirements.txt): python verify_release.py, then python tests/test_r10.py. Full reconstruction: python reproduce_all.py --outdir NEW_EMPTY_DIR, then python compare_reproduction.py NEW_EMPTY_DIR. This work was carried out independently by the author. It was not conducted within, funded by, or supervised by any program at Georgetown University, and the University bears no responsibility for its content.

items.summary: This record provides reproducibility materials supporting the manuscript “Actual-use verification and lineage-resolved fidelity in scientific AI”. The study evaluates scientific-AI fidelity by distinguishing assigned scientific objects, realized scientific objects, lineage or pathway fidelity, terminal scientific fidelity and claim boundaries.   The archive contains detailed evidence registries, comparison specifications, provenance and audit records, structured source records, manuscript source materials, display assets, and code for assembling and rendering the supplied publication materials. It also preserves the available historical CoralTemp/Coral Reef Watch daily-classification source excerpt used in the documented evidence chain.   The released materials support inspection of the reported evidence, scientific-object assignments, realized-use verification, lineage-resolved comparisons and presentation-level reproduction. They do not constitute a complete executable end-to-end reproduction of all scientific analyses. Complete raw-input and terminal-reference payloads, full benchmark execution and scoring pipelines, original scientific figure-generation programs and the original pinned scientific execution environments are not included. Public upstream scientific products and their provenance are documented in the manuscript and archive.   The archive should therefore be interpreted as a provenance-rich reproducibility and audit package rather than as a general benchmark of scientific-AI accuracy or reliability.
items.title: Reproducibility materials for "Actual-use verification and lineage-resolved fidelity in scientific AI"

items.summary: Evidence for large-scale differential rotation in the early universe and forward generation of its CMB topology by a primordial magnetic source — v1.8 reproducibility release Canonical 3° AC* is applied to the Planck PR3 SMICA, NILC, Commander, and SEVEM temperature reconstructions. AC* is a support-indexed multiscale spatial reconstructibility operator; direction, topology, and physical rotation arise only downstream. For canonical SMICA, 36,459 valid supports yield 27 large semiarcs. A separate high-resolution route uses 151 reciprocal HR1–HR2 structures to reconstruct an axis-free spherical tangent field. Blind recovery finds exactly four critical points of the represented lmax = 4 field: two spiral foci, one Node, and one Saddle. An all-sphere interval/Krawczyk analysis establishes completeness of this zero set. Focus A and Focus B are distinct oppositely rotating structures and admit a common transverse regular-vector realization in the coupled Einstein–Boltzmann state at recombination. Together with the differential-rotation reconstruction, polarization consistency, four-map comparison, perturbation tests, robustness controls, and exact propagation to z = 0, this provides evidence for large-scale differential rotation in the early universe. The independent forward-source test propagates a near-scale-invariant primordial magnetic source with nB = −2.9 to synthetic CMB skies and applies the same reconstruction without using the observed temperature map, critical-point geometry, Focus-A/Focus-B positions, measured H(J), or a magnetic-amplitude fit. One coordinate-blind realization generates the measured 2F+N+S topology and both rotational foci. The B-associated synthetic focus differs from the observed B focus only in the sign of a small divergent component; exact critical-point geometry is not reproduced. In eight matched phase-realization pairs, complete reconstruction occurs in five near-scale magnetic cases and none of the causal-white comparator cases, with three ties. The result establishes forward-generative capacity of the tested primordial magnetic source for the measured CMB topology and its two-focus rotational structure. It does not determine a unique magnetic spectrum, exclusivity among all possible source mechanisms, or an ensemble occurrence rate, and it is not a direct magnetic-helicity test. The release contains four public objects: Rambold_2026_CMB_v1p8.pdf — scientific manuscript. CMB_v1p8_interactive_scientific_viewer.zip — interactive scientific viewer. CMB_v1p8_python_pipeline.zip — executable analysis and replay code. CMB_v1p8_reproducibility_records.zip — scientific products, replay evidence, source-generation records, provenance, licences, manifests, SHA-256 bindings, and integrity records. Planck and WMAP FITS products are not redistributed and remain available from their public archives. Author-created scientific text and derived materials are released under CC BY 4.0 where applicable; original author-created software is released under the MIT License unless stated otherwise.
items.title: Evidence for large-scale differential rotation in the early universe from multiscale full-sky CMB reconstruction and forward generation of the reconstructed topology by a primordial magnetic source

items.summary: This record contains the public reproducibility package supporting the study “Persistent spatial organization and period-dependent associations in Beijing’s surface thermal–moisture environment”. The package includes the model-ready analytical dataset, temporal-screening and provenance records, cross-validation folds, model parameters and random-seed records, formal scripts for pooled and period-specific XGBoost–SHAP analyses, GeoDetector analysis, stored model outputs, quality-control and checksum records, and selected figure-source materials. The study comprises seven quality-controlled summer observation periods: 2000, 2004, 2005, 2009, 2010, 2016, and 2019. The primary reproducibility target of this package is the reported statistical analysis beginning from the archived ModelReady dataset. Production scripts preserve the original execution paths used during the formal analysis; users reproducing the analyses should update input and output paths to their local repository location. Upstream geospatial preprocessing scripts are retained for methodological provenance and may require the original third-party source products and local GIS configuration. Original Landsat, GLC_FCS30D, WorldPop, and Copernicus DEM source archives are not redistributed in this record and should be obtained from their respective providers. Detailed package structure, provenance, execution scope, and reproducibility notes are provided in the included README. Licensing: Data, documentation, and other original research materials created by the authors are released under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0) license. Source code created by the authors is released under the MIT License. Third-party and derived source materials remain subject to the terms of their original providers and are not relicensed by this record.

items.summary: Computational reproducibility package for the study “Uncertainty-aware medical decision support using feature-value graph-augmented rough granules.”   The archive contains the complete Python source code, public UCI benchmark data snapshots and metadata, exact repeated cross-validation split indices, preprocessing and discretization records, conventional and calibrated baseline outputs, rough-granular predictions and decision statuses, granule-support and attribute-reduction outputs, one-factor-at-a-time sensitivity analyses, corrected repeated-cross-validation statistical comparisons, final manuscript tables, and risk–coverage figures.   The study evaluates the Heart Disease, Breast Cancer Wisconsin Diagnostic, and Parkinsons benchmark datasets using repeated stratified 5-fold cross-validation with 10 repetitions. The feature-value graph is constructed from the measured attributes and is not an external biomedical knowledge graph. The package is provided for methodological verification and computational reproducibility and is not intended for clinical diagnosis or treatment.
items.title: Reproducibility package for uncertainty-aware medical decision support using feature-value graph-augmented rough granules

items.summary: This Zenodo record is a permanently preserved version of a PREreview. You can view the complete PREreview at https://prereview.org/reviews/22983291 . General assessment This manuscript addresses an important and underappreciated problem in computational chemistry and molecular machine learning: apparent differences in predictive performance can arise from benchmark construction and target definition rather than from intrinsic superiority of one modelling approach over another. The distinction between literature-reported absorption maxima and calculated vertical excitation energies is scientifically important, and the emphasis on genuinely external validation is a clear strength of the work. However, I find the central conclusion stronger than the evidence presently described appears to support. The results convincingly show that model performance changes substantially across datasets and label conventions. They do not yet demonstrate that label definition, rather than model capability, is the principal cause of the apparent machine-learning advantage over TD-DFT. Several factors change simultaneously across the comparisons presented in the manuscript, including chemical domain, dataset provenance, transition assignment, computational protocol, sample size, and the nature of the machine-learning representation. These factors make it difficult to isolate label definition as the causal explanation. The manuscript raises a valuable methodological concern, but the title and several conclusions should either be moderated or supported by additional controlled analyses. Major comments 1. The title makes a stronger causal claim than the study design appears to establish The title states that benchmark label definition, "not model capability," explains the machine-learning advantage over TD-DFT. This is a strong exclusionary claim. The results show that the apparent ranking between a Gaussian-process model and quantum-chemical calculations changes between evaluation datasets. However, label definition is not the only property that changes between these datasets. Their chemical composition, source literature, distribution of chromophores, spectral range, experimental conditions, and possibly computational protocols also differ. Therefore, demonstrating that a GP performs differently on a dataset with transition-specific labels does not by itself establish that label definition is the cause of the difference. A substantially stronger test would use the same set of molecules with two alternative target definitions—for example, a literature-reported overall λmax and an independently assigned transition-specific λmax—and evaluate both methods against both labels. A paired analysis of this type would isolate label definition while holding molecular distribution constant. Unless such a controlled analysis is provided, I suggest moderating the central conclusion to state that label definition and dataset provenance are important contributors to the reported ML advantage rather than demonstrating that they fully explain it. 2. One Gaussian-process model cannot represent "machine-learning capability" generally The machine-learning side of the comparison is represented by a Gaussian process using 256-bit Morgan fingerprints. This is a relatively specific and comparatively simple model representation. The conclusions therefore apply directly to this GP/fingerprint model, but not necessarily to molecular machine learning more broadly. Modern λmax prediction methods may use larger fingerprints, graph neural networks, message-passing architectures, pretrained molecular representations, three-dimensional information, explicit solvent descriptors, or quantum-chemical features. Such models may respond differently to both chemical and label distribution shifts.
